 ...Respondent(S):
 Petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India praying that in the
circumstances stated in the affidavit filed therewith, the High Court may be
pleased topleased to issue a Writ, or direction more particularly one in the
nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the Respondents in
intending to take possession of the petitioner's land admeasuring Ac. 3.46
cents in Sy. No. 95 of Prasannayapalli Village, RapthaduMandal, Anantapur
District for laying of road through .the petitioner's agriculture land without any
notice and proceedings prescribed under the Right to Fair Compensation and
Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
as illegal, arbitrary, Unconstitutional, against principles of natural justice and
contrary to the provisions laid down under Act 30 of 2013 and consequently
direct the respondents not to lay the road over the petitioner's land an extent
Ac. 3-46 cents in Sy. No. 95 of Prasannayapalli Revenue Village of
RapthaduMandal, Anantapur district, without following due process of law and
to pass
Ia No: 1 Of 2020
 Petition under Section 151 Cpc praying that in the circumstances stated
in the affidavit filed in support of the petition, the High Court may be pleased
pleased to direct the respondent authorities not to proceed with the laying of
road through the petitioner's land an extent of Ac. 3-46 cents in Sy. No. 95 of
Prasannayapalli Revenue Village of RapthaduMandal, Anantapur district
without following due process of law, pending disposal of the Writ petition
before this Hon'ble court and to pass
Counsel for the Petitioner:
 1. M L Neelima
Counsel for the Respondent(S):
 1. Gp For Panchayat Raj Rural Dev
The Court made the following:
 3
Order:

Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that, by virtue of efflux of time, the cause in the writ petition has become infructuous on the ground that the authorities have already laid road in the petitioner's land.

It is further submitted that the petitioner now intends to claim compensation and to take appropriate steps in that regard, and therefore sought permission of this Court to close the Writ Petition with liberty to pursue the said remedy.

In view of the fact that the road has already been laid in the petitioner's land and the petitioner Vennapusaumabhaskar Reddy vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 2 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111385135/
2 intends to claim compensation by approaching the authorities concerned, giving liberty to the petitioner in that regard, the Writ Petition is closed.
